answer: Down-regulation of genes primarily drives the metabolic effects of CBD treatment in CRC cells. In the primary comparison (CBD_IC50 vs DMSO vehicle, n=3/group) at padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 0.5, 429 genes were down-regulated vs 293 up-regulated (down/up ratio 1.46). GO Biological Process enrichment (hypergeometric/Fisher + Benjamini–Hochberg) showed that down-regulated — and not up-regulated — genes were significantly enriched for glycolytic process (GO:0006096, padj = 7.0×10⁻⁶, OR = 30.8) and glucose metabolic process (GO:0006006, padj = 2.5×10⁻⁴, OR = 18.3), driven by reduced expression of the glucose transporters SLC2A1/GLUT1 (log2FC −0.85) and SLC2A3/GLUT3 (−0.70), HK2 (−0.61), GPI (−0.67), ALDOC (−0.62), PGK1 (−0.52), and PDK1 (−0.69) (all padj < 0.00005). Only 7/125 (5.6%) annotated metabolic genes were DE-down vs 1/125 (0.8%) DE-up. This same metabolic down-signature was reproduced in both sensitivity comparisons (CBD_IC50 vs Untreated: 2 significant down terms, 0 up; serum-starved CBD vs serum-starved DMSO: 4 significant down terms vs 1 up) and by an edgeR-paradigm common-dispersion cross-check (up/down Jaccard 0.72/0.67). Conclusion (within the curated metabolic GO-BP terms, the study's main limitation): CBD's metabolic effect in CRC cells is primarily driven by down-regulation — specifically repression of glucose-uptake/glycolytic genes — not by up-regulation.
